This is the real perf lever the audit is circling.\n\n2. **[MED — lifecycle gap the 16-finding review missed] `RAFPlayback.drive()` has no generation guard — the exact double-schedule class `loop()` was hardened against.** The review fixed `loop()` with a `_gen` counter so a `stop()`+restart mid-async-frame cannot re-arm a second rAF chain (`playback.ts:73, 168-187`, called out in commit `7fc60e5`). But `drive()` (`playback.ts:142-159`) uses only the `if (this._rafId !== null) return` idempotency guard and never touches `_gen`. `drive`'s `frame` callback is *synchronous* (no `await`), so the in-flight-async-frame race that bit `loop` cannot occur identically — **but** the asymmetry is a latent trap: `drive`'s guard is `_rafId !== null`, and `stop()` bumps `_gen` + nulls `_rafId`, so a `frame` that has *already captured* its closure and is executing when `stop()`+`drive()` interleave (possible if a `tickDt` or `onFrame` callback re-enters `setTarget`→`_startLoop`→`drive` synchronously) will see `_rafId` freshly repopulated by the restart and schedule on top of it. Spring/smooth `_onFrame` callbacks are consumer-supplied and *can* re-enter. **Disposition: BOOK.** **GESTALT fix:** give `drive` the same `_gen`-captured reschedule check `loop` has (`const gen = ++this._gen; … if (gen !== this._gen) return;`), or — cleaner — fold `drive` and `loop` into one generation-guarded primitive since both are \"schedule frame, conditionally reschedule.\" The three-method split (`play`/`drive`/`loop`) is itself slightly over-shaped; `play` is `loop` + a clock + the reduced-motion gate, `drive` is `loop` + a settle-check. One guarded core with three thin entry shapes would delete the divergence that let `drive` miss the guard.\n\n3. **[MED — naming incoherence the `Tickable` unification hid] `tick` / `tickDt` / `tick(dt)` mean four different things across the light steppers; the `Tickable` interface unifies only `tickDt`.** `SmoothProgress.tick(): number` takes no arg (frame-rate-*dependent*, fixed damping, `smooth.ts:106`); `SmoothProgress.tickDt(dt): number` takes **ms** (`smooth.ts:128`); `SpringProgress.tick(dt): number` takes **seconds** (`spring.ts:204`); `SpringProgress.tickDt(dt): number` takes **ms** (`spring.ts:221`, a units adapter over `tick`); `Timeline.tick()` takes none (`timeline.ts:129`). So `obj.tick(16)` means \"advance 16 seconds\" on a spring but \"advance one damping step, arg ignored\" on a smoother — a foot-gun for a consumer treating them polymorphically. The `Tickable` interface (`playback.ts:30-35`) only standardizes `tickDt(dt): void` + `settled`, which is correct for the driver but leaves the public `tick` surface incoherent. Also `Tickable.tickDt` is typed `: void` while both implementors return `number` (`smooth.ts:128`, `spring.ts:221`) — harmless (covariant) but signals the interface was retrofitted, not designed-through. **Disposition: BOOK.** **GESTALT fix:** make `tickDt(dt: number)` (ms) the *single* canonical step on every stepper and the only public one; demote `SmoothProgress.tick()` (the frame-dependent no-arg variant) and `SpringProgress.tick(dt-in-seconds)` to private/internal or delete them in favor of `tickDt`. `springLinearStops.ts:64` and `springTimingFunction.ts:88` call `spring.tick(dt)` in seconds internally — those become `tickDt(dt*1000)` or a private `_stepSeconds`. One step method, one unit, across all four — the unification the `Tickable` interface implied but didn't finish.\n\n4. **[MED — fail-explicit contract half-honored] `setColorSpace` and `setHueMethod` silently bypass the `parseOption` seam they belong to.** The fail-explicit invariant (`errors.ts`, all nine other setters at `engine.ts:488-655`) is \"present-but-malformed throws `AnimationOptionError`; only genuine `undefined` defaults.\" But `setColorSpace` (`engine.ts:657-662`) does `colorSpace ?? defaultOptions.colorSpace` — a malformed *present* value (e.g. `setColorSpace(\"srgbbb\")`) is accepted and written, no throw. `setHueMethod` (`engine.ts:664-669`) writes any non-`undefined` value unchecked. # keyframes.js vs the 2026 animation-library landscape — SOTA research report

## §1 Internal evidence (what kf actually is, per the J audits + source)

**Public surface** (`src/animation/index.ts`): a proof-gated static/dynamic boundary. LIGHT static barrel (zero value.js edge, gated by `proof:boundary`): `NumericAnimation`, `SmoothProgress`, `SpringProgress`, `springLinearStops`, `springTimingFunction`, `ElementMorph`, `Timeline`/`ScrollTimeline`/`ManualTimeline`/`createNativeTimeline`, `RAFPlayback`, plus the E→I 16-export orchestration tier (`stagger`, `flip`/`flipShared`, `drag`/`Draggable`, `decay`/`decayRest`, `Sequence`, `resolveEasing`/`toEasing`, typed errors). HEAVY behind `loadAnimationEngine()`: `Animation`, `CSSKeyframesAnimation`, `AnimationGroup`, `animate`, `MotionPath`, `DrawSVG`, 30+ presets, `resolveKeyframes`.

**Recorded engine qualities** (audits at `docs/tranches/J/audit/{engine-core,engine-periphery,perf-frontier,scope-adversary}.md`):
- **Zero-alloc hot path** — real but narrower than claimed: `interpFrames` (binary-search seed, in-place lerp, stable-key null-fill) and `transformFramesGrouped` are genuinely zero-alloc and test-gated; two escapes remain: ENG-3 (group `_advanceSlice` allocates a `Promise.all` array every frame, `group.ts:501-513`) and ENG-4 (per-frame closure pair in `withReducedMotion`, `engine.ts:876-880`).
- **`advanceTo` canon** — `tickDt(dt)` vs `advanceTo(t)` is clean (zero bare `tick(`), but `advanceTo` is `async` — the FB-2 microtask hop has ridden 4 tranches (F→I) un-measured; J.W6 is LAND-or-KILL.
- **WAAPI delegation** — default ON (`useWAAPI: true`), correctness-first eligibility (`waapi.ts`): rejects ALL viewport/container units + `%` (with a principled `offset-distance` exemption), `calc()`/`var()`, color interpolation, non-uniform easing; queryable `waapiIneligibleReason`; emits spring `linear()` CSS twins through `Easing.css`.
- **`scheduler.yield`** — live-probed `yieldToMain()` (`internal/scheduler.ts`); `AnimationGroup.YIELD_BATCH = 32` batches child ticks for INP relief; gated by the LoAF bench (200-cell group, zero &gt;50 ms blocking tasks).
- **Static/dynamic boundary** — 16 KB ESM entry + 36 KB engine chunk (uncompressed; NOT directly comparable to competitors' min+gzip figures), light-only consumers never pull the parser or value.js.
- **Reduced motion** — ONE `withReducedMotion` gate; snap-to-rest-frame terminal path identical to forwards completion; SSR-safe.
- **Release posture (scope-adversary §1)** — npm is **frozen at 4.1.0**; the entire 16-export orchestration tier (Tranches E→I) has never been published; README teaches 4 of ~13 primitives; `flip`/`drag`/`draw-svg` have zero live demo coverage (EP-3).

## §2 External landscape (June 2026)

|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Ownership/license** | Webflow-owned (acq. Oct 2024); 100% free incl. all formerly-paid plugins (SplitText, MorphSVG, DrawSVG, ScrollTrigger, ScrollSmoother, Inertia) since Apr 2025 — but **proprietary "Standard License"**, not OSS; forbids Webflow-competing tools; revocable | **MIT**, independent, supporter-funded | **MIT** | n/a |
| **Engine** | rAF main-thread only; single ticker; no hardware acceleration | **Hybrid**: WAAPI + native ScrollTimeline first (compositor/120fps), JS fallback for springs/interrupts/gestures | Own rAF engine + optional `waapi` module | WAAPI; CSS scroll-driven animations (`scroll()`/`view()`) **still not Baseline** — Chrome/Edge + Safari 26, Firefox behind a flag; `@starting-style` Baseline; `linear()` Baseline Widely Available 2026-06-11; same-document View Transitions Baseline Newly Available Oct 2025 |

| **Perf claims** | Legacy "20× faster than jQuery"; no published ticks/sec | "2.5× faster than GSAP from unknown values, 6× at unit conversion"; compositor-immunity to main-thread jank is the headline | "lightweight/fast" positioning, no hard numbers | compositor-thread by construction |

## §4 Verdicts

**Genuinely AHEAD (things none of the big three do):**
1. **CSS `@keyframes` as a parseable, round-trippable source of truth** — parse author CSS, animate anything (DOM or plain objects), serialize back from the declared template. GSAP/Motion/anime all use proprietary tween syntaxes; the closest external thing (KeyframeKit-class utilities) parses into WAAPI only, with no arbitrary-object engine and no round-trip. This is kf's defining axis. (Skeptical caveat: the J audit found the per-card serializer still on the pre-transposition DOM-resolved path — ENG-1, P1 — so the round-trip claim has one live defect at one seam.)
2. **Perceptual color interpolation by default** — oklab default + CSS Color 4 `hueMethod`, multi-space via value.js. GSAP animates oklch incorrectly per its own forums; Motion and anime mix in RGB. Only the CSS platform itself matches this.
3. **Weighted layer blending** (`AnimationGroup` `replace`/`add`/`weighted`) — a compositor-style lerp-by-weight blend tier no mainstream JS library exposes; WAAPI's `composite` has add/accumulate but no weighted.
4. **Container-query-unit animation** with epoch-keyed DOM resolution (`cq*`/`calc`/`var` contract) — no competitor addresses container units at all.
5. **Engine-discipline proof culture** — gate-enforced zero-alloc hot path, boundary gates, LoAF/INP gates with `scheduler.yield` batching. Competitors claim; kf proves in CI. (This is an engineering-quality axis, not a user-capability axis.)

**BEHIND (honest):**
1. **Scroll orchestration** — kf has a scroll *progress driver* and a native-timeline wrapper; it has nothing in ScrollTrigger's class (pin, scrub smoothing, snap, enter/leave toggles, batch). Motion and anime also beat kf here. This is the single largest capability gap.
2. **SVG morph + full motion-path sampler** — both explicitly BOOKED out to value.js (VJ-F1) and unshipped; GSAP/Motion/anime all have path morphing and JS path samplers. kf ships only the CSS-native slivers.
3. **Ecosystem, docs, distribution** — the decisive non-capability gap: npm frozen at 4.1.0 while a GSAP-class API sits unpublished in source; README documents 4 of ~13 primitives; `flip`/`drag`/`draw-svg` have no demo; no framework adapters; zero community. By any "state of the art *as a product*" reading, this disqualifies SOTA status today.
4. **Drag/text/layout depth** — kf drag is 1-axis input plumbing vs GSAP Draggable/anime `createDraggable`; no text splitting (GSAP SplitText is now free); single-element FLIP vs Motion's shared layout animations.
5. **Compositor offload breadth** — kf's WAAPI eligibility is deliberately conservative (all `%`/viewport/container units and any color interp stay on rAF), so in practice most real animations run main-thread; Motion's hybrid delegates far more.

**PARITY:** springs (kf's ODE + velocity re-seat + `linear()` twin ≈ Motion; both beat GSAP's none), stagger, basic timeline sequencing, decay/inertia, SVG draw, tree-shaking story (kf's light/heavy boundary ≈ anime's subpaths ≈ Motion's tiers), reduced-motion handling (≈ Motion, ahead of GSAP), MIT licensing (≈ Motion/anime, ahead of GSAP's revocable proprietary grant).

## §5 Perf posture comparison

- **GSAP**: no published engine numbers; positioning rests on two decades of main-thread ticker tuning (lagSmoothing, single rAF). Architecturally capped: zero compositor offload, so it loses whenever the main thread is busy.
- **Motion**: publishes adversarial micro-claims ("2.5× faster than GSAP from unknown values, 6× at unit conversion" via deferred keyframe resolution) and the structural claim — hardware-accelerated animations are immune to main-thread jank. Their own tier-list concedes rAF/GSAP wins at "thousands of small elements."
- **keyframes.js (measured, `bench/` + b16 + G audit)**: `interpFrames` 2-frame opacity ≈ **996k ops/s**; threaded interp buffer at 600-frame windows: K=2 34.1k hz / K=5 18.3k / K=12 8.4k; LoAF gate holds a **200-cell AnimationGroup composite with zero &gt;50 ms blocking tasks** (YIELD_BATCH=32); demo steady-state 60 fps on cube under 4× CPU throttle (b16 — demo hotspots were Vue reactivity, not the engine). These are honest local vitest/playwright numbers, not public cross-library benchmarks.
- **kf's known soft spots (audit-recorded)**: FB-2 — `advanceTo` is `async`, imposing a microtask hop per frame in group/sequence drive (4 tranches deferred, J.W6 probe-or-KILL); ENG-3/ENG-4 — two per-frame allocation escapes outside the zero-alloc gates; PF-8 — value.js `lerpArray` SoA is unconsumed while the measured real-world K is 6–10, where SoA bites **2.5–4×** (value.js probe: 0.73× K=1 → 3.13× K=8 → 4.14× K=16) — a known, quantified perf reserve left on the table.

## §6 Synthesis line for the orchestrator

keyframes.js is **architecturally SOTA-class and uniquely positioned on three axes no 2026 competitor occupies** (CSS-@keyframes round-trip as source of truth, perceptual oklab interpolation, weighted layer blending), with engine discipline (proof-gated zero-alloc, conservative-correct WAAPI delegation, `scheduler.yield` INP batching) that exceeds what GSAP/anime demonstrate and matches Motion's hybrid rigor in spirit. It is **not SOTA as a shipped product**: it lacks the ScrollTrigger-class scroll tier, SVG morph, and any ecosystem — and its strongest tier (the 16-export orchestration surface) is literally unpublished (npm 4.1.0 freeze). Verdict shape: *ahead on parsing/color/composition, parity on springs/stagger/sequencing/inertia, behind on scroll orchestration/morph/ecosystem; perf credible but with three audit-named reserves (FB-2, ENG-3/4, lerpArray SoA) unspent.*

     ```js
     import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
     import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
     import { dirname, resolve } from "node:path";
     import { cpus } from "node:os";
     const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
     const flag = (name, def) => { const a = argv.find((x) => x.startsWith(`--${name}=`)); return a ? a.slice(name.length + 3) : def; };
     const workers = Math.max(1, Number(flag("workers", Math.max(1, Math.min(8, cpus().length - 2)))) || 1);
     const pkgPath = resolve(flag("pkg", "package.json"));
     const cwd = dirname(pkgPath);
     const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pkgPath, "utf8"));
     const tiers = argv.includes("--all") ? ["proof:correctness", "proof:hygiene"] : argv.filter((a) => a.startsWith("--tier=")).map((a) => a.slice("--tier=".length));
     // ... parses each tier's && chain into leaves; worker pool runs `sh -c leaf`; summary prints "RUN-ALL FAILED: <leaf>" + "RUN-ALL ALL GREEN"; process.exit(1 iff any failed)
     ```
     Uses cursor-based worker pool; `spawn("sh", ["-c", leaf], { cwd, stdio: ["ignore", "inherit", "inherit"], env })`.

# S.A0 follow-up — the two Linux CI causes, closed

## 1. `proof:cold-entry` clause (b) amiga — the cold-race, fixed in SOURCE

**Reproduced (not assumed):** pressing the dock play the instant the button exists under CDP `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate: 20` on the built dist reproduced the runner signature **byte-identical** — aria Play→Pause (flipped), slider null→0, started=false — plus the discriminating fingerprint the runner log lacked: **`machine.perScene.amiga.playing` stayed `false` after the press**.

**Verified mechanism (diverges from the hypothesis's "group arming" guess — C-20):** the amiga group is built synchronously and is never empty; the real seam is the **scene machine's reducer**: `PLAY` is inert while `status === "loading"`, so on a slow device the gesture landing before SCENE_READY was **silently dropped** while the transport's optimistic local `isPlaying` flipped the aria. SCENE_READY then read `snap.playing=false` → paused → the engine never started. Fast macOS arms before the gesture — why it only red on the runner.

**The gestalt cure — the gesture is honored, three seams, no gate changes:**
1. `stores/sceneMachine.ts` — PLAY during `loading` **QUEUES** the intent onto the snapshot (status never jumps ahead of the arm); PAUSE during loading **withdraws** it; SCENE_READY's existing `snap.playing` read consumes the queue.
2. `stores/scenePlaybackAdapters.ts` — the group adapter's `restore()` treats the queued-fresh snapshot (`playing:true, animations:{}` — only the pre-arm queue is ever empty) as a **START** (`group.play()`), not an eight-field re-seat; a withdrawn queue rests (K4-C cold default holds).
3. The **machine→transport intent edge** (`App.vue` → `EditorShell.vue` → `AnimationControlsGroup.vue`, new optional `machinePlaying` prop): a residual observed live after 1+2 — engine running + machine playing + aria stuck "Play", because `group.started` flips only on the first rAF tick and the transport's identity-watch sampled it stale. The machine's `playing` status now flows down; the transport syncs its ref to that truth (immediate, equality-guarded; playground omits the prop).
4. `test/scene-machine-reducer.test.ts` — the "inert in loading" case encoded the reproduced defect as law; re-derived to the queue semantics (C-20), two new cases assert queue+arm and withdraw.

**Verified:** the 20×-throttle early-press probe starts the engine from the queued intent (slider advancing by t+4s, zero pageerrors); **exit 0** on: `cold-entry` (all clauses incl. amiga direct-hash + the hero clause (a)), `fsm-suspend-resume-live`, `subject-animates`, `scene-machine-irrefragable`, `control-surface-single-writer`, `single-toggle`, `live-session` (full battery), reducer/DFA/identity unit tests, `tsc`.

# glass-ui audit → keyframes.js Tranche U redesign

Repo: `/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui` · `@mkbabb/glass-ui@4.2.0` · current branch `tranche/BG` (with `docs/tranches/BH/` planning the 5.0.0 cut). Vue 3.5 + reka-ui + Tailwind v4 + Vite 8 + Vitest 4.

---

## 1. THE POST-BH COMPONENT-SET IDIOMS

The governing doctrine is **FEATURE-DIR COLOCATION (AY.W-COLOCATE)**, stated verbatim in `CLAUDE.md:100`:

&gt; "a complex component is a sub-component dir — components at root, composables under `composables/`, constants in `constants.ts`, shaders in `shaders/`, skeletons in `skeleton/` (each 'if needed'), + a `README.md`. Enforced by `proof:colocation`."

**Every component is a directory** (never a flat file). Two families: `src/components/ui/` (43 dirs — reka-primitive wrappers) and `src/components/custom/` (49 dirs — house components). Directories are **kebab-case**; files inside are **PascalCase.vue**; the barrel is always `index.ts`.

### Leaf — `ui/button/` (flat, 2 files)
```
src/components/ui/button/
├── Button.vue        (13.9 KB — CVA-consumed via index)
└── index.ts          (17.1 KB — the buttonVariants cva() lives HERE, not in the SFC)
```
Idiom: even a "leaf" keeps a dir. The CVA variant table lives in `index.ts` (`export const buttonVariants = cva(...)`, `button/index.ts:5`), NOT in the SFC — the SFC imports it. `Button.vue` has **zero `&lt;style&gt;` blocks**; all styling is Tailwind utility classes composing shared glass recipes (`.btn-pill`, `.glass-capsule`, `.tap-squish`) defined centrally.

### Mid — `ui/tabs/` and `ui/select/` (flat multi-SFC + barrel)
```
src/components/ui/tabs/          src/components/ui/select/
├── Tabs.vue                     ├── Select.vue          (409 B — thin reka re-wrap)
├── TabsList.vue                 ├── SelectTrigger.vue   (7.8 KB — the heavy one)
├── TabsTrigger.vue              ├── SelectContent.vue
├── TabsContent.vue              ├── SelectItem.vue  ... (10 SFCs total)
├── TabsIndicator.vue            └── index.ts
└── index.ts
```
`tabs/index.ts` is a pure re-export barrel (5 `export { default as X } from './X.vue'` lines). `TabsIndicator.vue` carries **no scoped style** — the elastic-indicator spring reads central `src/styles/segmented-tabs.css`. Note the custom **`SegmentedTabs`** at `custom/tabs/` is the public tabs surface; `ui/tabs` is described as "off the public surface" (`CLAUDE.md:158`).

### Mid-complex — `custom/easing/` (colocation with composables/ + constants + README)
```
src/components/custom/easing/
├── EasingPicker.vue           (14.7 KB, 0 &lt;style&gt; blocks)
├── EasingConfigurator.vue
├── composables/
│   └── useEasingPicker.ts     (12 KB — the hook lives in composables/, one file)
├── constants.ts               (curve catalogue / mode constants)
├── README.md                  (per-component doc — colocation "if needed")
└── index.ts                   (re-exports SFCs + the composable + 6 types)
```
`easing/index.ts:5-14` re-exports the composable AND its types from the barrel (`useEasingPicker`, `EasingPickerMode`, `EasingPickerValue`, …). This is the "types-through-the-barrel" idiom (SFCs can't re-export types, so `constants.ts`/composables own them). Doc-canon at `CLAUDE.md:621` records the boundary law: the picker COMPOSES value.js math, owns only the chassis.

### Complex — `ui/drawer/` (composables/ + context module + constants)
```
src/components/ui/drawer/
├── Drawer.vue  DrawerContent.vue  DrawerOverlay.vue
├── DrawerHeader.vue  DrawerFooter.vue  DrawerTitle.vue  DrawerDescription.vue
├── composables/
│   ├── useDrawerSnap.ts          (16.3 KB — the snap engine)
│   └── drawerSnapContext.ts      (2 KB — provide/inject DI module)
├── constants.ts                  (3.4 KB)
└── index.ts                      (2.6 KB — re-exports SFCs + 3 union types + reka pass-throughs)
```
`drawer/constants.ts` is the model example of the **colocated constants home**: module-scope magic numbers (`DRAWER_SNAP`, `BOTTOM_SHEET_LADDER`, `DRAWER_FLING_VELOCITY`, `DRAWER_SNAP_LABEL`) + a pure helper `resolveDefaultSnapPoints()` live there rather than at the top of the composable (`constants.ts:1-8` states the convention "mirroring dock/constants.ts"). The DI context module imports its `Symbol()` label from `constants.ts` so it's typed once. `drawer/index.ts` exports the union types (`DrawerDirection`, `DrawerMode`, `DrawerStage`) plus re-exports reka primitives renamed (`DialogPortal as DrawerPortal`).

### Most complex — `custom/dock/` (sub-component dir + composables/)
```
src/components/custom/dock/
├── GlassDock.vue  DockSection.vue  DockLayerGroup.vue  DockLayer.vue
├── DockIconButton.vue  DockTabButton.vue  DockSelectTrigger.vue ...
├── composables/     # useDockState, useLayerTransition
└── index.ts
```
Descriptor **types live in `constants.ts`** (the "SFC-cannot-re-export-a-type colocated home" — `CLAUDE.md:691`, `:705`). Renderers &gt;~450 lines get carved OUT of the SFC into a colocated `composables/useX.ts` (`CLAUDE.md:132`: fourier-field → `composables/useFourierField.ts`; aurora → `useAurora.ts`; goo-blob → `useMetaballRenderer.ts`), enforced by `proof:no-god-module` (&lt;500-line ceiling, with a shader-literal exemption).

### Shared cross-component home — `ui/_shared/`
```
src/components/ui/_shared/
├── axes.ts               # BH.W-AXIS-GRAMMAR — Size/Orientation/Motion/Surface grammar types
├── useControlSize.ts     ├── useMotionAxis.ts     ├── useSurfaceAxis.ts
├── menuItemVariants.ts   ├── useStalePropWarning.ts
├── ModalOverlay.vue      └── index.ts
```
So there are **two composable homes**: (a) per-component `composables/` dir for hooks bound to one component; (b) `_shared/` for cross-component control-axis grammar + hooks. Truly generic composables (motion, glass, color, sidebar, virtual…) live in the top-level `src/composables/` tree (11 sub-dirs), NOT under components.

**Naming summary:** kebab-case dirs · PascalCase `.vue` files, component prefix repeated (`DrawerHeader`, `SelectTrigger`) · `index.ts` barrel per dir · `constants.ts` for typed constants/enums/pure helpers · `composables/useXxx.ts` for hooks · optional `README.md`, `shaders/`, `skeleton/`. **CSS is not colocated** — see §4.

## 2. IS `@` A DIRECTORY? — No. It is an alias only.

`find . -type d -name '@'` returns **nothing** (checked repo-wide and under `demo/`). glass-ui has no on-disk `@` directory. Unlike keyframes.js's `demo/@/`, glass-ui uses a **3-plane alias `@glass`** (introduced BH.B2.0 to decouple ~700 deep-relative `../../src/...` imports from src depth). The alias must be declared in all three planes because none reads the others:

| Plane | File | Mapping |
|---|---|---|
| Type | `tsconfig.json` `compilerOptions.paths` | `"@glass/*": ["./src/*"]` |
| Runtime (dev/build) | `vite.config.ts` `resolve.alias` | `"@glass": resolve(__dirname, "src")` |
| Test runner | `vitest.config.ts` `resolve.alias` | `"@glass": fileURLToPath(new URL("./src", …))` |

`vitest.config.ts:26-35` explicitly documents "vitest does NOT read vite.config.ts's alias" — hence the twin. `components.json` carries the shadcn aliases separately (`"components": "src/components"`, `"utils": "src/utils"`).

**src/ top-level layout** (`src/`):
```
src/
├── index.ts            # vueuse-FREE root barrel (14.8 KB)
├── api/                # 854L discovery aggregator (/api subpath) — SLATED FOR DELETION in 5.0.0
├── components/{ui,custom}/   # + components/ui/_shared
├── composables/        # 11 sub-trees (color, context, dark, dom, glass, keyboard,
│                       #   motion, reactive, sidebar, sortable, virtual)
├── subpaths/           # ~79 one-line mirror barrels — SLATED FOR DELETION in 5.0.0
├── styles/             # central CSS system (see §4)
├── types/  utils/  fonts/
└── axes.ts carousel.ts dark.ts forms.ts keyboard.ts motion.ts motion-core.ts
    sidebar.ts tokens.ts infinite-scroll.ts   # 12 curated flat top-level barrels
```

## 4. TOOLCHAIN NOTES (stay homogeneous with these)

**Build:** Vite `^8` with **Rolldown** (`rolldownOptions`, not `rollupOptions`) in `vite.config.ts`. Library build via `vite.library.ts`:
- `libraryEntries()` has **two tiers**: (1) ~12 hand-curated multi-line barrels that stay at `src/` top level; (2) every `src/subpaths/*.ts` batch-resolved by globbing the dir — "a new subpath barrel never has to be hand-added." Output format ES-only; `fileName`: `index → glass-ui.js`, else `&lt;entry&gt;.js`.
- Every runtime peer is `external` (`libraryExternal`: vue, reka-ui, @vueuse/core, @mkbabb/keyframes.js, @mkbabb/value.js, @mkbabb/pencil-boil, class-variance-authority, clsx, embla-carousel-vue, @lucide/vue). Machine-locked by `proof:external-payload`.
- `build` script = `vite build &amp;&amp; npm run emit-types`. Types are emitted **out-of-band by `vue-tsc`** (no in-Vite dts plugin): `emit-types` = `vue-tsc --project tsconfig.build.json &amp;&amp; node scripts/flatten-subpath-types.mjs` (`emitDeclarationOnly`, flat per-entry `.d.ts` into `dist/`).
- There is a **fleet of Vite configs** by concern: `vite.config.ts` (dev+lib), `vite.library.ts`, `vite.style-assets.ts`, `vite.style-fold.ts`, `vite.utility-emit.ts`, `vite.iter.config.ts`. Style assets are folded into the dist CSS by the `publishStyleAssets()` plugin.

**Export surface:** **per-component subpath exports** — ~90 keys in `package.json` `exports` (`.`, `./button`, `./drawer`, `./easing`, `./tokens`, `./styles`, `./styles/fonts`, `./fonts/*`, …), each mapping to a built `dist/&lt;name&gt;.js`. `typesVersions` mirrors them. This is a **many-subpath** model, not a single barrel — the root `.` barrel is deliberately vueuse-FREE, and vueuse/keyframes/value.js-bearing leaves are pushed OFF the root barrel onto their own subpaths (SCC-closure discipline).

**Test:** Vitest `^4` (`vitest.config.ts`), env `happy-dom`, `globals: true`. **Tests are NOT colocated** — since AV.W14, all tests live under top-level `tests/` mirroring `src/` (`tests/components/{ui,custom}/`, `tests/composables/...`, `tests/scripts/`); `proof:no-test-in-src` enforces zero test files in `src/`. Include globs: `tests/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,tsx,vue}` + `scripts/**/*.{test,spec}.ts`. Setup: `tests/setup.ts`. `resolve.conditions: ["development","module","browser","default"]`. There is also a separate `tests-visual/` workspace (Playwright π-capture) and a `tests/*.smoke.spec.ts` public-surface suite (`public-surface.spec.ts`, 24 KB).

**Lint/format:** **None in the conventional sense** — no `.prettierrc`, no `.eslintrc`/`eslint.config.*`, no prettier/eslint in devDependencies, no `prettier` key in `package.json`, no `lint`/`format` scripts. Code style is enforced instead by a **bespoke gate battery**: ~200+ `proof:*` npm scripts (e.g. `proof:colocation`, `proof:no-god-module`, `proof:external-payload`, `proof:subpath-classify`, `proof:phantom-classes`, `proof:no-layout-animation`, `proof:claude-structure-sync`) driven by `scripts/*.mjs`, plus `.githooks/commit-msg`. `typecheck` = `vue-tsc --noEmit &amp;&amp; vue-tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json`. TS config: strict, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `isolatedModules`, `moduleResolution: bundler`, ES2022 target — named exports + `import type` only (canon `docs/canon/conventions.md`).

**CSS conventions:** **Central `src/styles/` tree, not colocated** (colocation is planned but only 9 sheets in 5.0.0's B2.6). `src/styles/index.css` is a documented **@import cascade** where "load order is load-bearing," organized as thin `@import` ROOTS over cohesion-domain partials each &lt;500 lines:
- `tokens.css` → `tokens/{color-radius, glass, shadow, scheme-motion, scheme-spring, sizing, light-dark, dark-arm, property-regs, …}.css` (CSS custom properties are the source-of-record for every visual axis; `@property`-registered motion tokens).
- `glass.css` → `glass/{surfaces, material, glass-capsule, glass-chip, rim, squircle, ladder, accent-tone, surface-axis, …}.css`.
- Component recipes are **central `.css` files** (`drawer.css`, `select.css`, `segmented-tabs.css`, `cards.css`, `dock/`, `icon-chip.css`, …) using `@layer components` (`index.css:84`, `:91`, `:140`). SFC `&lt;style scoped&gt;` is used in only **47 of 253 `.vue` files** — and the representative components (Button, Drawer, DrawerContent, TabsIndicator, EasingPicker) carry **zero `&lt;style&gt;` blocks**, styling entirely via Tailwind utilities that compose the shared glass recipes. Font payload is split into `styles/fonts` (base64 woff2) off the critical `./styles` path. Idiom home documented at `docs/precepts/design-idioms.md` (`@theme` aliases → theme.css, `@utility` recipes → cohesion-domain file).

### Bottom line for Tranche U
- Adopt **feature-dir colocation**: every component is a kebab dir with PascalCase SFCs, an `index.ts` barrel, `constants.ts` for typed constants/enums/pure helpers, and a `composables/useXxx.ts` for any per-component hook; carve renderers &gt;~500 lines out of the SFC.
- Types flow **through the barrel** (SFCs can't re-export types) — put unions/enums in `constants.ts` or the composable and re-export from `index.ts`.
- Use a **`@`-style alias to `src/`** (glass-ui's is `@glass`) declared in **all three planes** (tsconfig paths, vite alias, vitest alias) — do NOT create an on-disk `@/` directory.
- **Tests in a top-level `tests/` mirror**, not colocated.
- **Per-component subpath exports** with a generated entry-set; keep the root barrel dependency-light and push heavy/peer-bearing leaves onto their own subpaths.
- CSS: **central `styles/` cascade** with token partials + `@layer components`, SFC scoped-style only where layering demands it.
- glass-ui's 5.0.0 direction is *fewer indirection layers* (kill mirror-barrel/aggregator sprawl, one generated export set, free renames like `goo-blob→blob`) — mirror that instinct in the U redesign.</result>

## Findings

**Two owner complaints → one dominant library bug + one secondary gap.**

### DEFECT A — the amiga sphere freezes ~2s into *every* play (the real bug)
Live demo: after pressing Play, `px`/`spin` advance until **t≈2000ms** then **freeze permanently** — `px` pinned at `+5` (WALL_X), `spin` at `π`, exactly the 25%-keyframe pose — while the FSM still says `playing:true`. `py` degrades to an erratic stutter. Reproduced identically in an **isolated built-engine harness**.

Root cause is a **library bug** in the `AnimationGroup` single-target compositor's plain-vars projection:
- `src/animation/compile/plain-vars.ts:109` caches a `ValueUnit[]` **leaf reference** (`writers.push({...units...})`); `:125` re-reads that cached ref every frame.
- But `src/animation/engine/interpolate.ts:194` **re-points** `_grouped[key]` to a *different* `AnimationFrame`'s leaf array when `t` crosses a keyframe segment boundary, and the projection (`group._plainProj`, `compositor.ts:172-182`) is only rebuilt on a **structural** change — never on a segment crossing. So it reads a now-orphaned, frozen leaf.
- The module docstring even encodes the false premise: *"built ONCE (structure is stable — only .value changes)."*

**Only amiga hits it** — it's the sole `singleTarget=true` + `unflatten=true` (custom object transform) group with multi-segment children. Cube (DOM/flat path) and square (`singleTarget=false` multi-target path) both dodge it — empirically confirmed: **cube round-trips and keeps animating**. Introduced by `efcb244` + `f060c17` (Tranche T, 2026-07-05), shipped green in 5.2.0.

### DEFECT B — scene suspend/resume
The **machinery is sound**: cube resumes+animates across a round-trip, easing (raw-rAF) suspends/resumes cleanly, **no orphaned-rAF accumulation** (playing amiga = 7 loops → leave = 1, probe gone), play-state preserved. The owner's "resume broken" is **Defect A wearing a mask** — the restored group re-seats past a segment boundary and freezes within ~1s. Genuine secondary gap: amiga's tab-visibility pause (`AmigaScene.vue:202-206`) governs only its WebGL render loop, never its animation-group simulation (machine `TAB_HIDDEN` is status-only), so the group clock drifts on hide → forward jump on return.

### Why the green gates missed it (vacuous-green)
- `proof:amiga-subject-is-pivot` → structural centering + drag-MAD within the first seconds.
- `proof:amiga-decay-visible` → the gesture-layer `omega()`, independent of the frozen group pose.
- `proof:fsm-suspend-resume-live` → FSM `playing`-flag round-trip + no-throw, **not** pixels-move-over-time.

None samples the autonomous bounce/spin past the **2000ms** boundary — the exact window where the freeze lives.

### Fix charter (in the dossier)
- **Fix A (library):** make `refreshPlainProjection` track the live `_grouped` leaf identity (store flat-key + source, re-resolve each frame) instead of a cached ref — the projection should be a *view*, not a *snapshot*. Add a born-RED gate that plays a `singleTarget`+`unflatten` ≥3-keyframe group past its first segment and asserts values keep changing, plus a `#/amiga` runtime gate sampling ≥3s.
- **Fix B (demo):** govern amiga's group *and* render loop under one suspend contract (fold the IntersectionObserver + visibility pause + machine TAB_HIDDEN), so suspend is symmetric and jump-free like the raw-rAF scenes.</result>
